sanskrit: brāhmaṇasthapatibhyāṃ ca nirmitaṃ yan niveśanam tad āvaset sadā prājño bhavārthī manujeśvara
english: A dwelling that has been built by a brāhmaṇa and by a master-builder—in such a one, O lord of men, let the wise man, desiring prosperity, ever take up his abode.

sanskrit: saṃdhyāyāṃ na svaped rājan vidyāṃ na ca samācaret na bhuñjīta ca medhāvī tathāyur vindate mahat
english: At the twilight hours, O king, the discerning man should not sleep, nor pursue his studies, nor take his meal; thus he wins long life.

sanskrit: naktaṃ na kuryāt pitryāṇi bhuktvā caiva prasādhanam pānīyasya kriyā naktaṃ na kāryā bhūtim icchatā
english: By night one should not perform the rites for the ancestors, nor groom oneself after eating; by him who desires prosperity, the offering of water should not be made by night.

sanskrit: varjanīyāś ca vai nityaṃ saktavo niśi bhārata śeṣāṇi cāvadātāni pānīyaṃ caiva bhojane
english: Parched barley-meal should ever be avoided by night, O Bhārata, as should be, at a meal, white leavings and water alone.

sanskrit: sauhityaṃ ca na kartavyaṃ rātrau naiva samācaret dvijacchedaṃ na kurvīta bhuktvā na ca samācaret
english: One should not eat to repletion by night, nor should one practise it; one should not pick one's teeth, nor do so after eating.

sanskrit: mahākulaprasūtāṃ ca praśastāṃ lakṣaṇais tathā vayaḥsthāṃ ca mahāprājña kanyām āvoḍhum arhati
english: A maiden born of a great family, commended, endowed with auspicious marks, and of fitting age—her, O greatly wise one, a man is worthy to wed.

sanskrit: apatyam utpādya tataḥ pratiṣṭhāpya kulaṃ tathā putrāḥ pradeyā jñāneṣu kuladharmeṣu bhārata
english: Having begotten offspring and so established his line, a man should give his sons over to the various branches of knowledge and to the duties of the family, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: kanyā cotpādya dātavyā kulaputrāya dhīmate putrā niveśyāś ca kulād bhṛtyā labhyāś ca bhārata
english: A daughter, when she is grown, should be given to a wise man of good family; sons should be settled in marriage, and servants should be taken from good households, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: śiraḥsnāto 'tha kurvīta daivaṃ pitryam athāpi ca nakṣatre na ca kurvīta yasmiñ jāto bhaven naraḥ na proṣṭhapadayoḥ kāryaṃ tathāgneye ca bhārata
english: Having bathed his head, a man should then perform the rites to the gods and to the ancestors; he should not perform them under the lunar mansion in which he himself was born, nor under the Proṣṭhapadās, nor under Agni's mansion (Kṛttikā), O Bhārata.

sanskrit: dāruṇeṣu ca sarveṣu pratyahaṃ ca vivarjayet jyotiṣe yāni coktāni tāni sarvāṇi varjayet
english: On all the harsh-natured days he should each day forbear; whatever days are named as such in the science of the stars, all of those he should avoid.

sanskrit: prāṅmukhaḥ śmaśrukarmāṇi kārayeta samāhitaḥ udaṅmukho vā rājendra tathāyur vindate mahat
english: Facing the east, with collected mind, one should have the trimming of the beard performed, or else facing the north, O king of kings; thus one wins long life.

sanskrit: parivādaṃ na ca brūyāt pareṣām ātmanas tathā parivādo na dharmāya procyate bharatarṣabha
english: One should utter no slander, neither of others nor of oneself; slander, it is declared, conduces not to righteousness, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: varjayed vyaṅginīṃ nārīṃ tathā kanyāṃ narottama samārṣāṃ vyaṅgitāṃ caiva mātuḥ svakulajāṃ tathā
english: He should avoid a deformed woman, and likewise a deformed maiden, O best of men—and one bearing the same lineage-name (gotra), or one born of his own mother's family.

sanskrit: vṛddhāṃ pravrajitāṃ caiva tathaiva ca pativratām tathātikṛṣṇavarṇāṃ ca varṇotkṛṣṭāṃ ca varjayet
english: An aged woman, one who has renounced the world, one devoted to another husband, one of too dark a hue, and one of a higher class than his own—these he should avoid.

sanskrit: ayoniṃ ca viyoniṃ ca na gaccheta vicakṣaṇaḥ piṅgalāṃ kuṣṭhinīṃ nārīṃ na tvam āvoḍhum arhasi
english: The discerning man should approach neither one unfit for wedlock nor one of an alien stock; a tawny-eyed woman or a leprous one you are not worthy to wed.

sanskrit: apasmārikule jātāṃ nihīnāṃ caiva varjayet śvitriṇāṃ ca kule jātāṃ trayāṇāṃ manujeśvara
english: One born in a family afflicted with the falling-sickness, and one base-born, he should avoid, and one born in a family of those marked with white leprosy—these three, O lord of men.

sanskrit: lakṣaṇair anvitā yā ca praśastā yā ca lakṣaṇaiḥ manojñā darśanīyā ca tāṃ bhavān voḍhum arhati
english: She who is endowed with auspicious marks and is commended for those marks, who is pleasing to the mind and fair to look upon—her you are worthy to wed.

sanskrit: mahākule niveṣṭavyaṃ sadṛśe vā yudhiṣṭhira avarā patitā caiva na grāhyā bhūtim icchatā
english: One should marry into a great family, or into one of like standing, O Yudhiṣṭhira; an inferior woman, or a fallen one, should not be taken by him who desires prosperity.

sanskrit: agnīn utpādya yatnena kriyāḥ suvihitāś ca yāḥ vedeṣu brāhmaṇaiḥ proktās tāś ca sarvāḥ samācaret
english: Having kindled the sacred fires with care, all those rites that are well ordained, that are declared by the brāhmaṇas in the Vedas, he should duly perform.

sanskrit: na cerṣyā strīṣu kartavyā dārā rakṣyāś ca sarvaśaḥ anāyuṣyā bhaved īrṣyā tasmād īrṣyāṃ vivarjayet
english: No jealousy should be harboured toward women, yet one's wife should be guarded in every way; jealousy shortens life, therefore one should put jealousy away.

sanskrit: anāyuṣyo divāsvapnas tathābhyuditaśāyitā prātar niśāyāṃ ca tathā ye cocchiṣṭāḥ svapanti vai
english: Sleeping by day shortens life, and so does lying abed when the sun has risen; so too lying down in the early dawn and in the night, and those who sleep while still unclean from food.

sanskrit: pāradāryam anāyuṣyaṃ nāpitocchiṣṭatā tathā yatnato vai na kartavyam abhyāsaś caiva bhārata
english: Adultery shortens life, and so does eating the barber's leavings; these things one should studiously refrain from, nor make a habit of them, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: saṃdhyāṃ na bhuñjen na snāyān na purīṣaṃ samutsṛjet prayataś ca bhavet tasyāṃ na ca kiṃ cit samācaret
english: At twilight one should not eat, nor bathe, nor void one's bowels; one should remain pure-minded at that hour and perform no other act whatever.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇān pūjayec cāpi tathā snātvā narādhipa devāṃś ca praṇamet snāto gurūṃś cāpy abhivādayet
english: Having bathed, O ruler of men, one should honour the brāhmaṇas, and, being bathed, bow down to the gods and salute one's elders.

sanskrit: animantrito na gaccheta yajñaṃ gacchet tu darśakaḥ animantrite hy anāyuṣyaṃ gamanaṃ tatra bhārata
english: Uninvited one should not go to a sacrifice, though one may go merely to behold it; for to go uninvited shortens life, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: na caikena parivrājyaṃ na gantavyaṃ tathā niśi anāgatāyāṃ saṃdhyāyāṃ paścimāyāṃ gṛhe vaset
english: One should not wander abroad alone, nor go forth by night; before the evening twilight has come, one should remain within the house.

sanskrit: mātuḥ pitur gurūṇāṃ ca kāryam evānuśāsanam hitaṃ vāpy ahitaṃ vāpi na vicāryaṃ nararṣabha
english: The command of mother, father, and elders is simply to be carried out; whether it seem beneficial or harmful, it is not to be questioned, O bull among men.

sanskrit: dhanurvede ca vede ca yatnaḥ kāryo narādhipa hastipṛṣṭhe 'śvapṛṣṭhe ca rathacaryāsu caiva ha yatnavān bhava rājendra yatnavān sukham edhate
english: In the science of archery and in the Veda effort should be made, O ruler of men, and on the back of the elephant, on the back of the horse, and in the handling of chariots: be diligent, O king of kings, for the diligent man thrives in happiness.

sanskrit: apradhṛṣyaś ca śatrūṇāṃ bhṛtyānāṃ svajanasya ca prajāpālanayuktaś ca na kṣatiṃ labhate kva cit
english: Unassailable by his foes, by his servants, and by his own kin, and devoted to the protection of his people, such a man suffers harm in no quarter.

sanskrit: yuktiśāstraṃ ca te jñeyaṃ śabdaśāstraṃ ca bhārata gandharvaśāstraṃ ca kalāḥ parijñeyā narādhipa
english: The science of reasoning you should master, and the science of grammar, O Bhārata, and the science of music too; the arts, O ruler of men, are to be thoroughly known.

sanskrit: purāṇam itihāsāś ca tathākhyānāni yāni ca mahātmanāṃ ca caritaṃ śrotavyaṃ nityam eva te
english: The ancient lore, the histories, and such tales as there are, and the deeds of great-souled men—these you should ever be listening to.

sanskrit: patnīṃ rajasvalāṃ caiva nābhigacchen na cāhvayet snātāṃ caturthe divase rātrau gacched vicakṣaṇaḥ
english: A wife in her courses one should not approach, nor summon; the discerning man should go to her, bathed, on the night of the fourth day.

sanskrit: pañcame divase nārī ṣaṣṭhe 'hani pumān bhavet etena vidhinā patnīm upagaccheta paṇḍitaḥ
english: On the fifth day a female is conceived, and on the sixth day a male; by this rule the learned man should approach his wife.

sanskrit: jñātisaṃbandhimitrāṇi pūjanīyāni nityaśaḥ yaṣṭavyaṃ ca yathāśakti yajñair vividhadakṣiṇaiḥ ataūrdhvam araṇyaṃ ca sevitavyaṃ narādhipa
english: Kinsmen, connections, and friends are ever to be honoured; sacrifice should be offered to the best of one's power with rites of manifold gifts; and thereafter the forest should be resorted to, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: eṣa te lakṣaṇoddeśa āyuṣyāṇāṃ prakīrtitaḥ śeṣas traividyavṛddhebhyaḥ pratyāhāryo yudhiṣṭhira
english: This summary account of the marks of long-life-giving conduct has been declared to you; what remains is to be learned from the elders versed in the three Vedas, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: ācāro bhūtijanana ācāraḥ kīrtivardhanaḥ ācārād vardhate hy āyur ācāro hanty alakṣaṇam
english: Right conduct is the begetter of prosperity; right conduct is the increaser of renown; from right conduct life itself is prolonged, and right conduct destroys every ill-omened mark.

sanskrit: āgamānāṃ hi sarveṣām ācāraḥ śreṣṭha ucyate ācāraprabhavo dharmo dharmād āyur vivardhate
english: Of all the scriptural traditions, right conduct is declared the highest; from right conduct springs dharma, and from dharma life is increased.

sanskrit: etad yaśasyam āyuṣyaṃ svargyaṃ svastyayanaṃ mahat anukampatā sarvavarṇān brahmaṇā samudāhṛtam
english: This, conferring fame, conferring long life, leading to heaven, a great means of well-being, was proclaimed by Brahmā out of compassion for all the classes of men.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yathā jyeṣṭhaḥ kaniṣṭheṣu vartate bharatarṣabha kaniṣṭhāś ca yathā jyeṣṭhe varteraṃs tad bravīhi me
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How an elder should bear himself toward his juniors, O bull of the Bharatas, and how juniors should bear themselves toward an elder—that tell me.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca jyeṣṭhavat tāta vartasva jyeṣṭho hi satataṃ bhavān guror garīyasī vṛttir yā cec chiṣyasya bhārata
english: Bhīṣma said: Bear yourself as an elder, my son, for you are ever the eldest; weightier is the conduct of the teacher than that of the pupil, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: na gurāv akṛtaprajñe śakyaṃ śiṣyeṇa vartitum guror hi dīrghadarśitvaṃ yat tac chiṣyasya bhārata
english: Toward a teacher of undeveloped wisdom a pupil cannot rightly conduct himself; for the far-sightedness that belongs to the teacher belongs not to the pupil, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: andhaḥ syād andhavelāyāṃ jaḍaḥ syād api vā budhaḥ parihāreṇa tad brūyād yas teṣāṃ syād vyatikramaḥ
english: At the time for being blind let even the wise man be as if blind, and at the time for being dull, dull; whatever transgression there be among such matters, he should point it out only with tact.

sanskrit: pratyakṣaṃ bhinnahṛdayā bhedayeyuḥ kṛtaṃ narāḥ śriyābhitaptāḥ kaunteya bhedakāmās tathārayaḥ
english: Men whose hearts are already estranged would, before one's very eyes, deepen what division has been wrought; tormented by another's prosperity, O son of Kuntī, and likewise foes who crave disunion.

sanskrit: jyeṣṭhaḥ kulaṃ vardhayati vināśayati vā punaḥ hanti sarvam api jyeṣṭhaḥ kulaṃ yatrāvajāyate
english: The eldest causes a family to flourish, or again brings it to ruin; the eldest may even destroy the whole family in which he is born.

sanskrit: atha yo vinikurvīta jyeṣṭho bhrātā yavīyasaḥ ajyeṣṭhaḥ syād abhāgaś ca niyamyo rājabhiś ca saḥ
english: But should an elder brother wrong his younger, he should forfeit his rights as eldest and his share, and he is to be restrained by kings.

sanskrit: nikṛtī hi naro lokān pāpān gacchaty asaṃśayam vidulasyeva tat puṣpaṃ moghaṃ janayituḥ smṛtam
english: For a man given to wrongdoing goes without doubt to evil worlds; like the blossom of the bamboo (vidula), his begetting is remembered as fruitless.

sanskrit: sarvānarthaḥ kule yatra jāyate pāpapūruṣaḥ akīrtiṃ janayaty eva kīrtim antardadhāti ca
english: In whatever family a wicked man is born, the source of every calamity, he begets only ill fame and makes good repute vanish away.

sanskrit: sarve cāpi vikarmasthā bhāgaṃ nārhanti sodarāḥ nāpradāya kaniṣṭhebhyo jyeṣṭhaḥ kurvīta yautakam
english: And all uterine brothers who follow forbidden courses deserve no share; nor, without first giving to his juniors, should the eldest set aside a portion for himself.

sanskrit: anujaṃ hi pitur dāyo jaṅghāśramaphalo 'dhvagaḥ svayam īhitalabdhaṃ tu nākāmo dātum arhati
english: A father's inheritance belongs to the younger as well; but as for the traveller, whose gain is the fruit of his own legs' toil, what he has won by his own striving he need not give away against his will.

sanskrit: bhrātṝṇām avibhaktānām utthānam api cet saha na putrabhāgaṃ viṣamaṃ pitā dadyāt kathaṃ cana
english: When brothers are yet undivided, even if their exertion be in common, a father should in no wise allot to a son an unequal share.

sanskrit: na jyeṣṭhān avamanyeta duṣkṛtaḥ sukṛto 'pi vā yadi strī yady avarajaḥ śreyaḥ paśyet tathācaret dharmaṃ hi śreya ity āhur iti dharmavido viduḥ
english: One should not slight one's elders, be one ill-doing or well-doing; whether a woman or a younger-born, if one perceive what is better, let one act accordingly—for the better is dharma, so they say, and so the knowers of dharma understand.

sanskrit: daśācāryān upādhyāya upādhyāyān pitā daśa daśa caiva pitṝn mātā sarvāṃ vā pṛthivīm api
english: A preceptor outweighs ten instructors, a father ten preceptors, and a mother ten fathers—or even the whole earth.

sanskrit: gauraveṇābhibhavati nāsti mātṛsamo guruḥ mātā garīyasī yac ca tenaitāṃ manyate janaḥ
english: In claim to reverence she surpasses all; there is no elder equal to a mother. Because the mother is the weightier, therefore do people so honour her.

sanskrit: jyeṣṭho bhrātā pitṛsamo mṛte pitari bhārata sa hy eṣāṃ vṛttidātā syāt sa caitān paripālayet
english: The eldest brother is equal to a father when the father is dead, O Bhārata; for he should be the provider of livelihood to these others, and he should protect them.

sanskrit: kaniṣṭhās taṃ namasyeran sarve chandānuvartinaḥ tam eva copajīveran yathaiva pitaraṃ tathā
english: The juniors should all bow down to him, following his will, and they should look to him for their support, just as to a father.

sanskrit: śarīram etau sṛjataḥ pitā mātā ca bhārata ācāryaśāstā yā jātiḥ sā satyā sājarāmarā
english: These two, the father and the mother, bring forth the body, O Bhārata; but the birth that the teacher fashions by his instruction—that is the true one, free from age and death.

sanskrit: jyeṣṭhā mātṛsamā cāpi bhaginī bharatarṣabha bhrātur bhāryā ca tadvat syād yasyā bālye stanaṃ pibet
english: An elder sister too is the equal of a mother, O bull of the Bharatas; and a brother's wife is likewise to be esteemed, at whose breast in childhood one may have drunk.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca sarveṣām eva varṇānāṃ mlecchānāṃ ca pitāmaha upavāse matir iyaṃ kāraṇaṃ ca na vidmahe
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Among all the classes, and even among the barbarian peoples, O grandsire, this inclination toward fasting exists; yet its cause we do not understand.

sanskrit: brahmakṣatreṇa niyamāś cartavyā iti naḥ śrutam upavāse kathaṃ teṣāṃ kṛtyam asti pitāmaha
english: By the brāhmaṇa and the kṣatriya the observances are to be performed—so we have heard; yet how does fasting come to be a duty for them, O grandsire?

sanskrit: niyamaṃ copavāsānāṃ sarveṣāṃ brūhi pārthiva avāpnoti gatiṃ kāṃ ca upavāsaparāyaṇaḥ
english: Declare the rule of fasts for all, O king, and what destiny he attains who is devoted to fasting.

sanskrit: upavāsaḥ paraṃ puṇyam upavāsaḥ parāyaṇam upoṣyeha naraśreṣṭha kiṃ phalaṃ pratipadyate
english: Fasting is the supreme merit; fasting is the highest refuge. By fasting here, O best of men, what fruit does one obtain?

sanskrit: adharmān mucyate kena dharmam āpnoti vai katham svargaṃ puṇyaṃ ca labhate kathaṃ bharatasattama
english: By what is one freed from unrighteousness, and how does one attain to righteousness? How does one win heaven and merit, O best of the Bharatas?

sanskrit: upoṣya cāpi kiṃ tena pradeyaṃ syān narādhipa dharmeṇa ca sukhān arthāṃl labhed yena bravīhi tam
english: And having fasted, what should be given thereafter, O ruler of men, by which, through righteousness, one might gain happiness and wealth—tell me that.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ kaunteyaṃ dharmajñaṃ dharmatattvavit dharmaputram idaṃ vākyaṃ bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo 'bravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: To the son of Kuntī, knower of dharma, son of Dharma, as he spoke thus, Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu, knower of the truth of dharma, said these words.

sanskrit: idaṃ khalu mahārāja śrutam āsīt purātanam upavāsavidhau śreṣṭhā ye guṇā bharatarṣabha
english: Verily, O great king, this was heard of old—what excellent virtues lie in the practice of fasting, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: prājāpatyaṃ hy aṅgirasaṃ pṛṣṭavān asmi bhārata yathā māṃ tvaṃ tathaivāhaṃ pṛṣṭavāṃs taṃ tapodhanam
english: For I once questioned Aṅgiras, descendant of Prajāpati, O Bhārata; just as you question me, so did I question that sage rich in austerity.

sanskrit: praśnam etaṃ mayā pṛṣṭo bhagavān agnisaṃbhavaḥ upavāsavidhiṃ puṇyam ācaṣṭa bharatarṣabha
english: Questioned by me with this very question, the blessed one, sprung from fire, set forth the meritorious rule of fasting, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: aṅgirā uvāca brahmakṣatre trirātraṃ tu vihitaṃ kurunandana dvistrirātram athaivātra nirdiṣṭaṃ puruṣarṣabha
english: Aṅgiras said: For the brāhmaṇa and the kṣatriya a fast of three nights is enjoined, O delight of the Kurus, and here also one of twice three nights is laid down, O bull among men.

sanskrit: vaiśyaśūdrau tu yau mohād upavāsaṃ prakurvate trirātraṃ dvistrirātraṃ vā tayoḥ puṣṭir na vidyate
english: But as for the vaiśya and the śūdra who out of delusion undertake a fast of three nights or of twice three nights, for those two no thriving comes of it.

sanskrit: caturthabhaktakṣapaṇaṃ vaiśyaśūdre vidhīyate trirātraṃ na tu dharmajñair vihitaṃ brahmavādibhiḥ
english: The skipping of every fourth meal is ordained for the vaiśya and the śūdra; the three-night fast is not enjoined for them by the knowers of dharma, the expounders of the Veda.

sanskrit: pañcamyāṃ caiva ṣaṣṭhyāṃ ca paurṇamāsyāṃ ca bhārata kṣamāvān rūpasaṃpannaḥ śrutavāṃś caiva jāyate
english: By fasting on the fifth and the sixth lunar days and on the full-moon day, O Bhārata, a man is born patient, endowed with beauty, and learned.

sanskrit: nānapatyo bhavet prājño daridro vā kadā cana yajiṣṇuḥ pañcamīṃ ṣaṣṭhīṃ kṣaped yo bhojayed dvijān
english: The wise man who keeps the fifth and the sixth as fast-days and feeds the twice-born, and is given to sacrifice, becomes never childless nor ever poor.

sanskrit: aṣṭamīm atha kaunteya śuklapakṣe caturdaśīm upoṣya vyādhirahito vīryavān abhijāyate
english: And by fasting on the eighth and on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight, O son of Kuntī, one is born free from disease and full of vigour.

sanskrit: mārgaśīrṣaṃ tu yo māsam ekabhaktena saṃkṣipet bhojayec ca dvijān bhaktyā sa mucyed vyādhikilbiṣaiḥ
english: He who passes the month of Mārgaśīrṣa taking but a single meal a day, and with devotion feeds the twice-born, is freed from diseases and sins.

sanskrit: sarvakalyāṇasaṃpūrṇaḥ sarvauṣadhisamanvitaḥ kṛṣibhāgī bahudhano bahuputraś ca jāyate
english: Filled with every blessing, possessed of all healing herbs, sharing in the fruits of tillage, rich in wealth and rich in sons—so is he born.

sanskrit: pauṣamāsaṃ tu kaunteya bhaktenaikena yaḥ kṣapet subhago darśanīyaś ca yaśobhāgī ca jāyate
english: He who passes the month of Pauṣa with but a single meal, O son of Kuntī, is born fortunate, fair to look upon, and sharing in renown.

sanskrit: pitṛbhakto māghamāsam ekabhaktena yaḥ kṣapet śrīmatkule jñātimadhye sa mahattvaṃ prapadyate
english: He who, devoted to the ancestors, passes the month of Māgha with a single meal a day attains to greatness in a prosperous family, in the midst of his kinsmen.

sanskrit: bhagadaivaṃ tu yo māsam ekabhaktena yaḥ kṣapet strīṣu vallabhatāṃ yāti vaśyāś cāsya bhavanti tāḥ
english: He who passes the month presided over by Bhaga (Phālguna) with a single meal a day comes to be beloved among women, and they become devoted to him.

sanskrit: caitraṃ tu niyato māsam ekabhaktena yaḥ kṣapet suvarṇamaṇimuktāḍhye kule mahati jāyate
english: He who, self-controlled, passes the month of Caitra with a single meal a day is born into a great family abounding in gold, gems, and pearls.

sanskrit: nistared ekabhaktena vaiśākhaṃ yo jitendriyaḥ naro vā yadi vā nārī jñātīnāṃ śreṣṭhatāṃ vrajet
english: Whoever, with senses subdued, passes through the month of Vaiśākha on a single meal a day—be it man or woman—attains pre-eminence among kinsmen.
